title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing & padding minimization (heuristics v21)
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Improves dynamic batching heuristics to reduce padding overhead and improve throughput/latency tradeoffs. No API changes. Backwards-compatible runtime behavior. Recommended rollout on Dedicated pools first.
description:
Context and motivation: We observe that a large portion of token compute is wasted due to padding when batching requests with heterogeneous sequence lengths. Previous heuristic iterations (v1..v20) introduced bucketing and basic pad-aware batching; this PR refines those heuristics to better handle long-tail seqlen distributions, reduce worst-case latency regressions, and guide kernel selection for quantized paths.

Summary of changes: - Introduce percentile-driven bucket boundaries computed from short-term request seqlen histogram (p10/p25/p50/p75/p90/p99) with smoothing and hysteresis to avoid thrash. - New padding cost model: cost_per_token = kernel_cost(seqlen) + pad_penalty * pad_tokens; pad_penalty calibrated per-device/arch. Buckets are chosen by minimizing estimated cost under SLO constraints. - Add dynamic bucket merging when bucket usage falls below threshold to avoid small-inefficient batches. - Integrate bucket hints with scheduler so worklets prefer same-bucket coalescing and enable kernel-specific fast paths for commonly seen bucket sizes (e.g., 64/128/256). - KV-cache awareness: prefer coalescing requests that share warm KV-cache entries; add a lightweight tag to requests indicating cache_age to bias batching decisions. - Continuous batching tweaks: lower the max wait time for short seqlens when system is under high tail latency to prioritize latency SLO. - Telemetry: emit seqlen_bucket, estimated_padding_saved, and chosen_kernel tags for per-route dashboards.

Commits summary: - 8a3f28a: add percentile-driven bucketing module and histogram collector - b2d7c19: implement pad cost model and bucket cost minimizer - c4e1f7d: scheduler integration + bucket-aware coalescing - d13b9fa: KV-cache tagging + warm-cache bias - e5a4b2c: continuous batching SLO-aware timing adjustments - f7c9d1e: telemetry and dashboards + docs update - 01be2f4: perf tests and microbench harness updates

Files changed (high level): - runtime/batching/bucketing.py (new): percentile histogram, bucket calculation - runtime/batching/pad_cost.py (new): pad cost model and calibration hooks - runtime/scheduler/coalescer.py: integrate bucket hints into coalescing logic - runtime/scheduler/kernel_router.py: add bucket->kernel hint mapping and fast path selection - runtime/kv/cache_tags.py: carry cache_age metadata on requests - observability/metrics/batching_metrics.go: new metrics and labels - docs/ops/batching.md: operational guidance and rollout notes - tests/perf/bucketing_bench.py: microbench harness and scenarios - examples/benchmarks/compare_v20_v21.yaml: workloads used for validation

Testing and CI: - Unit tests: new coverage for bucketing math, pad cost model, and scheduler integration. - Perf regressions: ran full perf-canary matrix on p4d and a100 pools. - Results: end-to-end throughput up by ~10% on mixed-seqlen workload (25th/50th/90th = 16/64/512) and padding tokens reduced by ~28% measured across the canary traffic. Tail (p99) latency improved by 6% for typical routes; in high long-tail routes (many very long sequences) we saw up to 12% throughput uplift after bucket merging. - CI status: all checks passed (build, lint, unit tests, perf-canary).

Review conversation (high level): - Maya Torres: "Can you clarify how hysteresis parameters are chosen? In noisy workloads this could cause oscillation." 
  - Author: "Added adaptive smoothing: we use EWMA on histogram buckets with alpha tuned per-route; defaults are conservative. See runtime/batching/bucketing.py lines 120-140 for defaults and comments."
- Evan Brooks: "Will KV-cache tagging increase request size/overhead significantly?" 
  - Author: "Tag is a single byte flag + 16-bit age bucket; negligible compared to payload. Included cost in perf tests."
- Samir Patel (perf owner): "Please add an operator toggle to revert to v20 for affected pools." 
  - Author: "Added feature flag runtime.config.dynamic_batching.version with rollout docs in docs/ops/batching.md. Ops can revert to 'v20' if needed."

Backward compatibility and safety: - No protocol/API changes. All runtime heuristics are behind a config flag and default to enabled gradually (Dedicated pools first). There is an operator toggle and a forced-fallback to previous strategy if padding cost model reports regression.

Merge notes: - Squash-and-merge to keep history small; included perf artifacts in release notes and linked Linear tasks. Rollout plan in docs/ops/batching.md recommends 10% canary on Dedicated pools for 72h before global enable.

Related work items: Linear ENG-4217 (dynamic batching roadmap), PERF-1123 (padding cost calibration), previous PRs: pr-94820, pr-93456, pr-91321 (iterative heuristics).
additional_context: This PR represents the next evolutionary step after the seqlen bucketing and padding-minimization series. We focused both on steady-state economic wins and worst-case latency protections. Operators should watch the new 'estimated_padding_saved' metric after rollout.
notes_for_release: Enable v21 heuristics behind feature flag by default for new deployments; recommend canarying on low-traffic Dedicated pools and monitoring estimated_padding_saved and p99 latency. No user-facing API changes.
changelog: Performance: improved dynamic batching heuristics to reduce padding (median 10% throughput uplift, up to 28% padding reduction on mixed workloads). Added telemetry and an operator rollback flag.
